gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 diagnoses an unsupported torus logarithmic-Sobolev/displacement-convexity justification and an undefined hypothesis parameter. It does not recognize the distinct incompatibility between quantifying over arbitrary L1 data and requiring an L2-trace solution.

Both entries identify the invalid inference from compact-resolvent/bounded perturbation information for a non-self-adjoint operator to a real spectral conclusion. ISSUE-003 also supplies the relevant consequence and a repair retaining only the justified compact-resolvent claims.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The proof does not establish self-adjointness or reality of the spectrum, so compact-resolvent perturbation results cannot justify the asserted real spectral structure.

component_coverage.gold_component: The perturbation argument preserves compact resolvent but does not establish self-adjointness or real spectrum.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly identifies the non-symmetric operator, the absence of a reality argument, and the possibility of complex eigenvalues.

component_coverage.gold_component: The real-spectrum proposition must be weakened or separately justified rather than inferred from compact-resolvent conclusions.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 states that only compact-resolvent and finite-multiplicity conclusions are established and proposes removing the unsupported real-spectrum inference.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 concerns an unstated hypothesis that the selected m eigenvalues exhaust the relevant half-plane. It does not identify the sign error changing the correct threshold from Re(eta)≤delta to the incorrectly used Re(eta)≤−delta.

Both entries identify that merely assuming H1 regularity for the shape function does not make div(mu grad alpha_j) an L2-valued map on H1. ISSUE-005 gives the same missing second-derivative/gradient regularity and a corresponding stronger assumption.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed H1-to-L2 operator mapping fails for H1 shape functions because the divergence expression need only be distributional; stronger regularity is required.

component_coverage.gold_component: H1 assumptions on mu and alpha_j do not establish that div(mu grad alpha_j) belongs to L2.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly expands the divergence and explains why alpha_j only in H1 is insufficient for the asserted L2 mapping.

component_coverage.gold_component: The generic controlled formulation therefore needs stronger shape regularity to define the operator.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 states that the operators are not well defined at the stated regularity and proposes a stronger regularity assumption.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify the replacement of the Fredholm orthogonality condition by the invalid non-membership-in-the-kernel-span condition. Both also note that the needed orthogonality follows from the zero-mean property and give that as the repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Solvability requires the forcing vector to be orthogonal to the kernel, not merely outside its span; the zero-mean eigenfunction supplies the required orthogonality.

component_coverage.gold_component: Fredholm solvability requires orthogonality to the kernel, whereas non-membership in its span is insufficient.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-007 states the correct self-adjoint solvability criterion and explains why the non-membership condition is neither necessary nor sufficient.

component_coverage.gold_component: The relevant zero-mean eigenfunctions satisfy the needed orthogonality, which should be used in the proof.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-007 explicitly derives the integral-zero orthogonality from membership in the zero-mean space and proposes replacing the criterion accordingly.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 independently diagnoses that the full-space Riccati equivalence and lift fail because the mass/complement decomposition used in the formula is wrong: P does not commute with L and the constant-vector lift is not the correct mass direction. This is the same substantive full-space-versus-zero-mean decomposition defect as I007, although ISSUE-004 presents it through the noncommutation and adjoint-control consequences rather than spelling out every compressed-generator term.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed extension and lifting of the reduced Riccati equation to the full space is not valid under the stated decomposition: the chosen complement/lift is wrong for a nonconstant target and the full-space dynamics must respect the appropriate projection and mass direction.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; ISSUE-004 demonstrates the same invalid full-space equivalence through the resulting noncommutation and incorrect mass-direction coupling rather than reproducing the displayed compressed-generator formula verbatim.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proposed complement and lift using the constant-function rank-one term do not represent the actual mass complement for a nonconstant target.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies the incorrect constant-vector term, states that the correct vector is the target density, and says the displayed lift/equivalence fails.

component_coverage.gold_component: The full-space Riccati construction must account for the projected dynamics and associated mass-component couplings; the old uncompressed extension is not equivalent to the reduced equation.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly diagnoses failure of the projection/decomposition equivalence and the resulting mass-component couplings, and proposes dropping or restricting the full-space equivalence while correcting the mass direction.
